summary: Gone 40-foot DNR lookout above Port Angeles: built 1953, wrecked by wind 1963, rebuilt 1964, abandoned 1968; Willhite finds communication towers on the summit.

facts.design: 40-foot wooden DNR live-in tower with a 14x14 cab on top
facts.status_note: Abandoned 1968 and now gone per FFLOS; Firelookout.com lists it as gone; Willhite describes the summit as full of communication towers

staffing.status: Manned in June 1957 and on a temporary basis in May 1963

access.note: Route on DNR land from Mt. Pleasant Road; Willhite calls the small gate likely open and advises parking on the main road without a Discover Pass; no official access rule found

visit.trail_note: About 2.5 miles with 1,635 feet of climb from a trailhead among houses on the outskirts of Port Angeles (Willhite); summit forested and full of communication towers

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Willhite and a Washington Lookouts photo caption give December 28, 1963; a January 14, 1964 newspaper notice says high winds on Christmas Eve wrecked the tower. The story reports both and does not pick one.

notes_for_editor: Brief record was accurate on status, height, elevation, county, coordinates and the 2012 registration; no corrections proposed. The 1963 wind wreck appears only in Willhite and the Washington Lookouts newspaper captions; one web search found no independent corroboration, and the FFLOS and Firelookout.com pages do not mention 1963. Access 'public' is inferred from Willhite's route notes; no DNR rule found. Two named individuals in the sources are left out as private people. Willhite calls the 1968 event a burglary; the newspaper calls it vandalism, so the event is marked other. The Washington Lookouts caption is dated December 28, 1963 but its text says High winds Tuesday; December 24, 1963 was a Tuesday and December 28 was a Saturday, so the caption wording points to Christmas Eve. The story gives the dates as the sources state them.
